reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the fluorine-induced Al2O3 formation and oxidation resistance in Ti-45Al-8.5Nb, but it provides no data on HfNbTaTiZr, nor on the retention of mechanical properties after treatment. The key premise that the effect transfers to a different alloy system and preserves mechanical performance is therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Fluorine treatment promotes formation of a protective Al2O3 layer on Ti–Al–Nb alloys at 1000 °C
The Al2O3 layer is continuous, adherent, and reduces oxidation weight gain
The treatment involves spraying/dipping in NH4F solution followed by isothermal oxidation
The protective oxide scale leaves bulk microstructure and mechanical properties intact
This fluorine effect can be transferred to the chemically distinct HfNbTaTiZr alloy
